segments.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין תְּרוּמַת שְׁנֵיהֶם תְּרוּמָה, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אִם תָּרַם הָרִאשׁוֹן כַּשִּׁיעוּר — אֵין תְּרוּמַת הַשֵּׁנִי תְּרוּמָה, וְאִם לֹא תָּרַם כַּשִּׁיעוּר — תְּרוּמַת הַשֵּׁנִי תְּרוּמָה.
segments.en: «Rabbi Akiva says: The teruma of neither of them is teruma.» Since each separated teruma independently, it is clear that neither accepts the separation of the other, and therefore neither is valid. «And the Rabbis say: If the first one separated teruma of» the correct «measure,» i.e., one-fiftieth of the produce, the produce is thereby tithed, and therefore «the teruma of the second is not teruma; but if» the first «did not separate teruma of» the correct «measure,» and he separated too little, «the teruma of the second is teruma.»
